Rohit Sati
--Revisionist
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and another
--Respondents
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Girish Chandra Lakhchaura, learned
counsel for the revisionist.
2. Mr. Shailendra Singh Chauhan, learned
D.A.G. assisted by Mr. Vikash Uniyal, learned Brief
Holder for the State.
3. By means of the present Revision, the
revisionist has assailed the order dated 07.08.2026,
passed by the Additional Principal Judge, Family
Court, Haldwani, District Nainital by means of
which interim maintenance of ₹15,000 has been
granted by the said Court to the respondent wife.
4. On a query made to the learned counsel for
the revisionist, he would submit that the monthly
salary as per his affidavit in compliance of
judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case
of Rajnesh vs. Neha is ₹63,000. However, a perusal
of the impugned order dated 07.08.2026 would
reveal that a specific finding has been recorded by
the Additional Principal Judge, Family Court,

UKHC010196642026
Haldwani that from the salary slip of the month of
December, 2023 of the revisionist, the revisionist is
serving in company by the name of Pidilite
Industries Limited in the capacity of Zonal Training
In-charge and he is drawing a salary of ₹73,109,
and even after the deductions, he is getting a net
salary of ₹67,932 per month.
5. Assailing the order impugned, the learned
counsel for the revisionist would submit that the
respondent wife is residing at her aunt's home
without any rhyme or reason on her own sweet will,
and therefore, the learned Additional Principal
Judge, Family Court erred by granting interim
maintenance and allowing the application for
interim maintenance and granting interim
maintenance of ₹15,000.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist further
submits that he is all along been ready and willing
to keep the respondent wife with him, and in fact,
he has earlier instituted a suit under Section 9 of the
Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court at
Lucknow, which unfortunately got dismissed for
non-prosecution; however, the restoration
application for the restoration of the said case is
pending.
7. Since it is not disputed that the respondent is
the wife of the revisionist, and it is also not disputed
that the monthly salary as per the own salary slip of
the revisionist is ₹73,109, and which upon
deductions, the net salary would be ₹67,932, this

UKHC010196642026
Court does not find any error in the impugned order
whereby interim maintenance to the tune of
₹15,000 has been granted by the Additional
Principal Judge, Family Court.
8. However, all the contentions as are being
raised by the learned counsel for the revisionist
would be available to him to be agitated in the main
maintenance application, and any observation made
hereinbefore will not come in the way of the final
adjudication of the application under Section 144 of
the BNSS.
9. In view of the aforesaid, there is no force in
the present Revision and the same is dismissed
accordingly.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.)
03.11.2026
